results.reason: Issue 1 quotes Supply Agreement §14.2: a change of more than 50% is deemed an assignment requiring Supplier's prior written consent, with a 30-day termination right. It notes Schedule 4.4 says 'None' and that the §7.2(c) closing condition is therefore automatically satisfied.
The response never mentions Supply Agreement §16.1, Vantrell's one-way right to assign without Customer consent, or the risk that the contract passes to a competitor.
Issue 2 calculates the 120-day deadline as about September 2, 2026 and notes the SPA is dated September 21, 2026. It concludes the option and the Extension Pricing have lapsed.

Issue 3 explains that Side Letter §2 limits Fundamental Reps to §§4.1 and 4.2 and that §11.11 gives the Side Letter priority. As a result, Capitalization and Taxes become subject to the deductible and the 10% cap.

Issue 4 identifies Side Letter §6.1/6.2 choosing Delaware law and the Court of Chancery against SPA §§11.8/11.9 (New York), and explains the resulting split. Side Letter precedence is established in Issue 3 rather than restated in Issue 4.
The response repeatedly refers to 'the 10% cap' alongside the $84.5M Purchase Price. It does not spell out '10% of the Purchase Price' or $8,450,000 for the cap, so this is a lenient pass.
The response states: 'Because the Side Letter has first priority under Section 11.11, its definition controls.'
The response is a memorandum to the Partner, with each issue listing documents and sections, 'Why it matters to Halvorsen,' and a recommendation.
Issues run from critical to low significance, and there is a dedicated section listing items requiring a client call.
The response states the option has lapsed and never suggests it remains exercisable.
The response correctly states that Capitalization and Taxes become capped and that the Side Letter controls.
